edge.title: The QR you scan to get paid
edge.setup: You're selling something online. The buyer says his app is acting up, so he sends a QR code or a payment request and tells you to scan it or approve it so the money lands. A few taps and a PIN later, your balance is lower, not higher.
edge.tell: You were asked for your UPI PIN to receive money.
move: Receiving money never needs your PIN. A PIN screen means money is leaving your account.
Read the screen before you type anything. If it says Pay, or shows an amount you are about to send, close it.
Offer your own QR or UPI ID and let the buyer pay you. A genuine buyer will.
If money has gone, call your bank immediately and report on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in the same day.
edge.why: UPI lets only the payer authorise a payment, with a PIN. Any step that asks the receiver for a PIN is the payer step in disguise. The con works by relabelling the direction of money, and the PIN is the one thing that cannot be faked.
edge.variants: Same shape: 'refund' links that ask for a PIN, collect requests labelled cashback, QR codes pasted on parcels or posters.

lens.name: Planning fallacy
lens.one_line: We estimate time and cost from the best-case plan, so projects almost always run late and over budget.
lens.detail: People picture the plan going smoothly and forget the delays that hit every real project: approvals, weather, supply, rework. Asking 'how long did similar projects actually take?' gives a far better estimate than asking 'how long should this take?'. It is the base rate applied to schedules.
elsewhere: Home renovations finishing weeks after the contractor's date.
Your own 'it will take ten minutes' tasks.
lens.test: What did the last three similar things actually take, and why would this one be different?
lens.today: Bangalore Mirror and Urban Acres both report that Namma Metro Phase 3 has hit another land hurdle. Phase 3 timelines were set from the clean version of the plan, and land acquisition is the delay that recurs on projects like it. Treat any announced opening date as the best case, and do not tie a house move or job change to it.

moved.what: Namma Metro Phase 3 has hit another land hurdle (Bangalore Mirror, Urban Acres).
moved.so_what: If you are weighing a home or job move around a Phase 3 corridor, plan on the metro arriving later than announced and make the commute work without it.

moved.what: Rice price is nearing ₹100/kg and Karnataka farmers are seeking a 2 tmcft 'water loan' (The Times of India).
moved.so_what: Expect the monthly grocery bill to rise. Compare per-kg rates across varieties before stocking up for the festival week.

moved.what: The Centre has scrapped the ₹2.5/litre petrol export duty and raised the diesel levy to ₹11.5 (The Times of India).
moved.so_what: This is a levy on exports, not on pump sales, and the report does not mention a pump-price change. No action now; watch your pump rate over the coming days.

moved.what: Special trains from Bengaluru to Tuticorin and Kannur have been announced for Deepavali (Deccan Herald).
moved.so_what: If you are travelling south or to Kerala for the festival, check IRCTC for these services now, because regular festival trains fill first.

moved.what: The Bengaluru-Mumbai Vande Bharat sleeper is reported to start on 1 November (NDTV), and tickets are already on the waiting list (The Indian Express). This morning's brief cited 3 November from Deccan Herald.
moved.so_what: The start date differs between sources, so confirm it on IRCTC before planning a trip around it, and expect to book early or take a waitlist.

moved.what: Bengaluru police have issued 19-point Deepavali safety guidelines and warned of legal action against violators (The Hindu).
moved.so_what: Read the list before you burst crackers or host a gathering, since breaking a rule can now mean legal action.

carry_over.prompt: A group shows daily gains and a 'mentor' sends you to an app where your profit grows on screen: what is the tell?
carry_over.answer: Your profit exists only on a screen run by the people asking for your next deposit, and getting money out needs another payment first.
